detail_text: Specifically, A.Laboratory control procedures are not followed: -During review of electronic data for [redacted] USP API, we observed multiple unreported sample injections prior to or after the official reported sample injections for Related Substances and Assay by HPLC testing that were not documented in laboratory batch records. API batches involved; - [redacted] included batch numbers. Specifically, on 12/20/2024, your analyst injected a blank and single injection for sample [redacted], with calculations during the current inspection resulting in OOS for assay, with calculated result a [redacted] % versus specification of [redacted] %. The official reported result documented in your laboratory batch records for [redacted] was performed on 12/22/2024, with reported result as [redacted] %. This batch was shipped to the U.S. Market. -When we asked one of your analysts why they performed an unreported injection prior to the official injection, the analyst stated that the owner of the firm provided the sample and asked them to perform the test. Review of this analyst's training record revealed no laboratory training on performing any testing operations, including chromatography testing, no cGMP training, and no data integrity training. -After discussion of these deficiencies with your QC Manager, he stated that "for export purpose we check for confirmation again and again." -Furthermore, we observed that your firm appears to be performing arbitrary in-process sampling. Per your firm's QC Manager, your firm does not always perform in-process sampling, only when the firm's owner provides samples to test. We observed no laboratory batch records or calculations for in-process sampling, no assigned batch numbers in the sample set to in-process samples, and no mention of in-process sampling in batch records. In sample sets reviewed, there is no way of determining what batch numbers of [redacted] USP API were tested from the electronic data. Your firm's QC Manager stated that they did not know what batches were tested. -Consequently, QA and QC do not review electronic data, nor does your firm have a procedure for review of electronic data for the [redacted] standalone HPLC and [redacted] standalone GC equipment. Similarly, your firm does not have a procedure for sample set and sample naming conventions. B.During our walkthrough of the QC laboratory on January 19, 2026, a discarded printout was found in a trash bin. After review, your QC Manager stated that the printout documented a Loss on Drying (LOD) test for [redacted] raw material, AR. No. [redacted] dated January 18, 2026.
